pcs.pc_description: Write a brief description of the products manufactured and add details corresponding to the brand's purpose, position, personality, and unique features like handmade, eco-friendly etc.
Identify the target audience for your products by taking factors such as age, location, gender, income level, education, and ethnic background into consideration.
Check for information about competitors selling similar products successfully and how to differentiate your branding from them.
Try to include a brand story containing brief information about the origin of this product, artisans etc.
Create a unique brand name with the above factors, a logo and a simple slogan.
Register the brand and copyright if necessary.
Ensure GST registration is done, as it's mandatory for selling most of the products.
Use consultants, vendors or agencies for assistance.
Calculate the variable costs (per product) by adding the cost of raw materials, labour, utility expenses, affiliated commissions etc.
Estimate the fixed cost of the business, e.g., rent, property tax, insurance, machinery, maintenance and depreciation.
Decide on the profit margin by considering fixed and variable costs.
Work out the target price for every product once the margin is decided {Generally, Target Price = (Variable cost per product) / (1 - your desired profit margin as a decimal)}
Compare the price with existing competitors in the market and keep your price flexible.
Take help from professionals to try various pricing methods, market trends, and demands.
Considering the above factors, create a price list for all the products manufactured.

• Produce visually appealing product images by following the below steps: • Arrange your products with proper background and lighting. • If you have photography skills and feel comfortable taking pictures by yourself and own a digital camera/ mobile phone with a high pixel ratio - set the camera to the highest resolution and take photos. • Click high-quality pictures from multiple angles and perspectives. • Hire a professional photographer if the above steps are complicated or the budget permits.
Write down the product features, benefits, technical specifications, original and discount prices, etc.
Categorise the products based on any one of the factors, e.g., specifications or uses or methods/ raw materials.
Organise the content and design a catalogue. Agencies may also be hired to design the catalogues.

pcs.pc_description: Start with a basic inventory with a surplus of finished goods and raw materials.
Categorise and organise stocks according to type, e.g., raw materials, packing materials, finished products etc.
Label and stack the goods according to categories, part numbers, colours, tools etc.
Monitor your stockroom regularly and dedicate an employee to inventory management if required.
Do physical inventory counting daily and tally the same periodically with the production, orders placed/ received etc.
Forecast the requirement according to orders and season and restock accordingly.
Record and maintain inventory on books. Effective inventory management is essential for accounting and analysing the flow of business.
Inventory management software can also be used for maintaining inventory and order management on a computer.
Organise and record finished products, vendor information, and orders received.
Create accurate purchase orders for offline orders and share them with customers.
Use the order management tool provided by E-commerce platforms effectively and monitor each order placed.
Ensure to fulfil the order is within the timeline provided by the E-commerce platforms and generate periodical performance reports using their seller services.
Plan your production according to the orders received.
In the case of orders received through multiple E-commerce platforms, integrate and maintain records for all orders placed, physically or by computer.
Track the payments received against each order and file GST accordingly.

pcs.pc_description: Collect information about the e-commerce platforms in which you want to sell the products.
Check details about becoming their seller by calling their customer care or browsing their website.
Find information about the different schemes/ plans offered and details on their profit share, margins, assistance in filing GST, packing, shipping etc.

Coordinate with the seller/ registration team of the e-commerce platform to collect more information on the above-mentioned aspects and whether the privileges given by the Govt of India (if any) are taken into consideration.
Check and arrange if any infrastructure requested by the e-commerce platform companies e.g., thermal printers.
Read all the terms and conditions laid by e- commerce platforms in detail like packing regulations, processing time, returns & refunds, etc. and seek assistance if clarity required.
Get all the information and documents required for registration ready.

Register online in the e-commerce platforms by filling out the relevant fields like contact details, store name, bank account details and uploading the necessary documents like Aadhaar, PAN, address proof, and GST registration.
If online registration is difficult, get assistance from the customer care/ seller team for completing the registration.
Start selling on a single e-commerce platform at a time to identify the difficulties and to adapt.
Check whether the offline price decided earlier is feasible, with all the additional included and the profit margin is achieved.

Compare the pricing decided by you with that of similar products available on the e- commerce platforms. If your product is unique or the first of its kind on the platform, the price can be decided taking only the above points into consideration.
Decide on the final online price for each item and categorize them.
Once the registration process is completed, login to your account to start listing your products.
Select the respective category or search option can also be used.
If the existing categories/ options do not match, create a new category.

Update on requested fields like product name, batch details (if any), Price, quantity available, origin, product description, dimensions, item condition, HSN code, country of origin etc. and upload the photos.
Additional help can be taken from customer care or seller team for listing.

Once the product is live on the platform, check whether the listing matches with that of the details entered earlier. Coordinate further with customer care or seller team if there are any discrepancies.
You will get regular notifications on the orders placed from the e-commerce platform on the registered contact details.
Login to the seller account and check frequently for new orders received.
Use filters or search options to find the status of orders received.
Check whether the order details match with that of the listing.
Contact customer care or seller team if there are any discrepancies.
Confirm the new orders received and update further information about pick up/ dispatch, tracking details, shipping date etc.
Generate and print the shipping label and invoice.
Pack the product according to the specifications given by the e-commerce selling company and place the invoice inside the package.
Ensure that the guidelines for packing and labeling given by the e-commerce platform are followed on each stage.
Stick the shipping label firmly on the outside of package.
Handover to the courier company and update the tracking details on the website if shipping is done by self.
Check whether any return or exchange requests are received in your login.
Arrange for pick up if the couriering was originally done from your end.
Dispatch the replacement item if it is an exchange request and wait for the returned item.
If it is a return request, process for a refund once the product is received in good condition.
Login to the seller login and check on the other features available in the account.
Coordinate with customer care or seller team to know how the seller performance is rated and the steps to improve.
Answer to the questions raised by the customers about products.
Generate various available reports to check on the performance, customer ratings/ reviews etc.
In case of negative reviews received from customers, take action to rectify the errors.
Check the reasons for returns, exchanges and fix any issues.
Monitor whether the payments are received on time, for the orders processed.
Implement new and innovative products, services that help improve customer satisfaction.

pcs.pc_description: Choose suitable packing materials according to the type of product (e.g., fragile items, food items), the courier company's/transporter's guidelines/ restrictions, weight, product dimensions, distance, weather conditions, transportation charges etc.
Cover the product with a plastic bag or shrink wrap to protect it from dust, spillage etc. and ensure it is labelled.
Place the product inside the exterior packaging, e.g., cardboard boxes, flyers, and poly bags.
Add appropriate cushioning with materials like bubble wraps, sealed air pockets, thermocol beads etc., to avoid damage during transport.
Seal the package securely so there are no gaps and check thoroughly.
Fix the waybill/ tracking details, labels, sender & receiver information, shipping label, invoice etc., according to the E-commerce platform/company's and the courier company's guidelines.
Collect details about courier companies currently servicing your locality.
Gather further information like a tariff, delivery speed, VAS, plans, doorstep pick-up, online tracking, customer service etc., offered by them and their rate of complaints.
Choose the best service provider in the above aspects and tie up with them to send couriers regularly.
Create a plan with backup courier companies and which company to choose for different delivery locations according to the tariff, urgency of deliveries etc.
If the E-commerce company requests products to be delivered to their fulfilment centre, warehouse etc., choose transporters accordingly.
Track the packages regularly until they are delivered to the customer, using the tracking number by checking the courier company's website tracking or calling their customer care.

pcs.pc_description: Identify the suitable sales channels for the products or services.
Develop a digital marketing strategy for promoting products and services.
Determine the budget for promotional activities.
Use a mix of promotional strategies, such as social media and point-of-sale promotions.
Prepare the promotional materials/medium and messages.
Analyse networks and formal/ informal sources of support available for business.
Identify potential business opportunities through the identified networks.
Identify social media channels and blogs with customers' presence for the enterprise's products or services.
Use digital marketing tools like email and Search Engine Marketing (SEM) to market products and services.
Follow Search Engine Optimisation (SEO) practices to improve the business's visibility and products/services on the relevant search engines.
Coordinate with the relevant experts or agencies if the above actions are complex.
Ensure the privacy and security of consumer data.
Confirm that the latest updates are accurate on social media and digital marketing platforms.
Ensure prompt and appropriate response to customers who contact due to marketing and ask for referrals.
Calculate the profit and loss performance of the business.
Analyse profitability and business performance trends.
Prepare and follow simple budgets.
Estimate the cash flow over a fixed period and the savings required to absorb sales fluctuation.
Analyse the actual cost w.r.t physical output and reduce the cost wherever possible.
Open a bank account and deposit funds. Avoid holding excess cash in the business unit.
Do simple interest calculations before taking a loan and always read the terms and conditions.
Choose nationalised banks for transparency and authenticity.
Avoid taking financial risks during the initial phase of business.
Get help from banks setting up online banking services, UPI and using debit cards.
Analyse various digital payment options and Set-up online payment methods.
Follow the do's and dont's issued by RBI for secure online transactions.
